chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Qasim ibn Urwa, from Abu al-Abbas and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When a group gathers to kill one man, the guardian (of the deceased) decides which one of them shall be killed — and it is not permitted for them to kill more than one.
Indeed, God, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'And whoever is killed unjustly, We have given his heir authority, so let him not be excessive in killing.'

key_terms.الْإِسْرَاف فِي الْقَتْل: Excess in killing — executing more than one person for one victim, explicitly prohibited by the Quranic verse cited
key_terms.الْعِدَّة: A group or number of people; here used for multiple perpetrators of a collective killing
key_terms.الْوَالِي: The guardian of the slain — in qisas law, the wali al-dam (blood-guardian/heir) who holds the right to demand retaliation or pardon
key_terms.سُلْطَان: Authority/power; in 17:33 refers to the legal authority of the heir to demand retaliation
key_terms.قِصَاص: Retaliation in kind (implied concept); the legal principle governing this ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling when a group collectively kills one person?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) issues a legal ruling on collective homicide (al-shirka fi al-qatl): when multiple individuals conspire to kill one person, the victim's heir (wali al-dam) may only execute one of the perpetrators in retaliation — not all of them. The ruling is grounded in Quran 17:33, which grants the heir authority over retaliation (qisas) but warns against excess. This reflects the classical Shia jurisprudential principle that retaliatory killing cannot exceed the original crime in number.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Qasim Bin Urwa, from Abu Al Abbas and someone else, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When a number gather upon killing one man, the guardians (of the deceased) decide which one of them they would like to kill, and it is not for them that they kill more than one.
Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [17:33] and whoever is killed unjustly, We have indeed Given to his heir authority, so let him not be excessive with regards to the killing’.
